 motogp.com 
 31 Oct 2026
 Share
 URL copied

 Copy Link
 -->
 It was a heroic attempt, but the Aprilia Racing rider won’t be able to race at Sepang
 He made a superhuman effort, but it’s official: Jorge Martin (Aprilia Racing) will not be able to race in the Malaysian GP. Just six days after breaking his wrist in Australia, the 2024 Champion and 2026 title contender returned to the track on Friday at Sepang, doing 12 laps in the morning session and then a few more in the afternoon before ending his day early, intending to recharge for more on Saturday.
 -->
 Bonora explains the plan for Martin after Malaysia withdrawal
 The Aprilia Racing Team Manager outlines the next steps as the #89 is forced onto the sidelines in Sepang
 Unfortunately, after more time on track in FP2 ahead of qualifying, it was confirmed: Martin has withdrawn from the event. The #89 will remain on the sidelines, targeting next time out for another shot at his return.
 The title fight, however, remains open. Currently at 10 points off the lead held by Marc Marquez (Ducati Lenovo Team), Martin’s worst case scenario if he misses this race weekend would be a 47-point deficit should Marc Marquez do the double at Sepang – and 111 will still be on the table.
